metadata.case_name: WONG SEE MO v. LAM NAM FUI AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: furniture maker / carpenter (sawing timber and assembling furniture)

injuries.description: Tip of left index finger amputated; deep laceration across distal joint of left middle finger connected with skin flap only; lacerations over terminal phalanx of left ring and little finger. Fractures of terminal phalanx of left index, middle, ring and little fingers. Revision amputation of distal phalanx of left index, middle and ring fingers was done.
source:
"The patient's general condition was satisfactory. Tip of left index finger was amputated. There was deep laceration across distal joint of left middle finger connected with skin flap only. There were lacerations over terminal phalanx of left ring and little finger.

Fractures of terminal phalanx of left index, middle, ring and little fingers were seen in X-ray.

Revision amputation of distal phalanx of left index, middle and ring fingers was done.

He was treated and discharged.

He was grantee 20 days’ sick leave from 20/8/86 to 8/9/86 inclusive."

"The grip in the left hand is 40 1bs compared to a previous one of 30 lbs. The grip in the right hand, is 60 1bs which is probably not as strong as before because it has not been used in furniture making for a while. The left index finger is as before with normal sensation but because the middle finger has lost part of the middle phalanx he finds it difficult to approximate and hold screws with his left index while the middle finger steadies the screw at the same time for him to utilise the screwdriver. Flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joint is 90 degrees, the metacarpophalangeal joint flexes 90 degrees which is within normal limits.

The middle finger - he complains of some pain but movements are as follows:

Proximal interphalangeal joint 60 degrees, distal interphalangeal joint 90 degrees.

The ring finger is as before and, therefore, he still has 18% impairment of the whole person and loss of earning capacity is as before at 19%."
injuries.icd_description: Other specified traumatic amputation of two or more fingers alone

manifestations.description: considerable initial shock and pain and further pain continuing at least until the time of treatment
tenderness of the tips of his index and ring fingers
pain on flexion of those fingers
loss of strength in all (left hand grip 30 lbs or later 40 lbs compared to right 70 lbs or 60 lbs)
difficulty to approximate and hold screws with his left index while the middle finger steadies the screw (difficulty using a screwdriver)
cannot peel fruit for his children
difficulty holding a bowl in his left hand when eating
played an occasional game of basketball but has no desire to play now because he feels he cannot because of his injured hand

treatments_received: Revision amputation of distal phalanx of left index, middle and ring fingers
Physiotherapy three times a week until October, 1986
Stitches removed two weeks after operation
Admission to hospital for one day

losses.description: Major loss is dexterity in the left hand resulting from amputations, lacerations and fractures

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty fastening clothing; cannot peel fruit for his children; difficulty holding a bowl when eating

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Played occasional basketball but has no desire to play now because he feels he cannot because of his injured hand
